audits.claim: Chilam Balam of Chumayel: Princeton record C0940 no. 4, 'between 1775 and 1800', acquired 1968; Roys (1933) introduction pp. 6-7 records a notation signed Juan Josef Hoil and dated 1782, which does not date every component of the compilation.
audits.source_locator: Roys (1933), The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel, Introduction, pp. 6-7, as archived by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (live sacred-texts.com returned HTTP 403 to this client)
audits.source_excerpt: We know from internal evidence that the Chilam Balam of Chumayel was compiled by Don Juan Josef Hoil ... his name signed to a notation written in the same hand as the rest of the book and dated 1782.
audits.retrieval_method: FetchURL of the Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshot (web/2023id_) of the sacred-texts.com Introduction page, a public archival copy of the public-domain 1933 text; no CAPTCHA or interstitial was defeated. dpul.princeton.edu and findingaids.princeton.edu both served bot-verification interstitials on direct fetch this pass and were left untouched, not bypassed.
audits.basis: Whole-claim support for the Roys-recorded component, read at the exact cited locator: the Introduction (retrieved pp. 3-13) states the notation is signed by Don Juan Josef Hoil, written 'in the same hand as the rest of the book' and dated 1782, with 'only a few interpolations added at later dates ... written in different hands' - i.e. one notation, one copying hand, and explicitly non-uniform hands, exactly the basis on which the entry refuses to let 1782 date every component. The same retrieved introduction carries the caveat the entry encodes: 'Although it dates only from the year 1782, the language suggests the Seventeenth Century much more than it does the Eighteenth' (p. 6), and the Chumayel is 'a compilation made from various earlier works, many of which were probably copied from still older books' (p. 9). The retrieved provenance chain (baptismal records 1832/1833 by Justo Balam; 1838 purchase by Pedro de Alcantara Briceño; loan to George B. Gordon 1910; University of Pennsylvania Museum facsimile 1913; missing from the Cepeda Library by 1918) also supports the §4 copy-chain framing 'copy date ≠ content horizon'. No contradiction to the entry; no erratum warranted.
audits.coupling_implication: Language/era coupling, and the specific discipline the claim encodes: the 1782 date binds to the copying hand and that notation, while the archaic language points earlier, so no component of the compilation - least of all its mythic or prophetic contents - may be dated from this single notation. Composition, compilation, and copy horizons must stay distinct. When the Princeton catalogue elements are verified, the 1775-1800 estimate is a separate copy-level institutional estimate and must not be merged with the 1782 notation or propagated to the other Chilam Balam books (Kaua, Tizimin, Mani).
audits.limits: Partial-scope statement, to keep support non-laundered: the Princeton elements of the compound claim (C0940 no. 4; 'between 1775 and 1800'; acquired 1968) were NOT re-verified this pass - both dpul.princeton.edu and findingaids.princeton.edu served bot-verification interstitials on direct fetch and were not bypassed, so those catalogue elements remain unresolved and must not be treated as confirmed by this audit. Roys' text was read in a Wayback archival copy, not the live sacred-texts.com page (HTTP 403 to this client); printed pp. 6-7 pagination is as marked on the archived page. WebSearch was quota-exhausted during this pass, so discovery ran on direct public URLs only.

audits.claim: Bonampak mural dating (dedication 791 CE) is standard [MB13], in §9 used for the garment-ensemble minimum-evidence rule (depicted scene plus material evidence).
audits.source_locator: David Stuart, 'Orienting Bonampak', Maya Decipherment, 30 April 2009, third paragraph
audits.source_excerpt: Two of Yajaw Chan Muwaan's monuments, Stela 1 (780 A.D.) and a lintel from Structure 1 (791 A.D.), exhibit carver's signatures citing artisans from the court of Yaxchilan.
audits.retrieval_method: FetchURL of the live Maya Decipherment post; the live Wikipedia 'Bonampak' article was also retrieved as a secondary pointer. Not retrieved: UT Press book page (historical HTTP 403; no Wayback snapshot at two URL forms), Mesoweb Bonampak URLs (HTTP 404 on three paths), Houston (2012) Cambridge abstract (HTTP 429, doi.org and Cambridge direct), Smarthistory essay (HTTP 403; no Wayback snapshot), World History Encyclopedia (HTTP 404). No bot wall was bypassed; DuckDuckGo and Mojeek search attempts were abandoned when both served their own bot challenges.
audits.basis: Adjacent support only, so the claim is neither confirmed nor contradicted and stays unresolved, on the meso-14 precedent (nearby but not identical date does not upgrade). The retrieved epigrapher's post anchors 791 A.D. to a lintel from Structure 1 (with Yaxchilan carver signatures) and 780 A.D. to Stela 1; the retrieved Wikipedia article describes Structure 1 as 'built at the end of the eighth century A.D.' and repeatedly cites Miller & Brittenham (2013) as the standard treatment ('seminal work ... thorough discussion on the murals'), corroborating [MB13]'s status as the standard study. But no retrieved text states the mural 'dedication 791 CE' as such or attributes that year to the murals on MB13's authority: 791 is confirmed here for the Structure 1 lintel, not yet for the murals or for §9's use of [MB13]. The entry's source-attributed framing therefore stands unchanged and no correction is warranted.
audits.coupling_implication: Scope discipline the claim itself encodes: even once the attribution is verified, the 791 CE dedication anchors Structure 1's mural program in time; §9 cites [MB13] only as a minimum-evidence rule (depicted scene plus material/technique evidence, never one image alone). The mural year must not become a uniform garment chronology: ensembles depicted in the 791 CE scenes are dated scenes, not a horizon for Maya dress, and any garment claim still requires its own material evidence per the rule.
audits.limits: The cited publisher record (UT Press, HTTP 403) and the two Mesoweb Bonampak feature URLs of the previous pass (HTTP 404, paths not re-identified) could not be read; Cambridge Core rate-limited (HTTP 429) on both doi.org and direct attempts; no Wayback snapshots exist for the UT Press book page or the Smarthistory essay; INAH's zone page served unrelated landing content. WebSearch was quota-exhausted this pass, so no search-engine discovery was available. The specific attribution 'dedication 791 CE, standard [MB13]' therefore remains unresolved and must not be upgraded from the retrieved lintel date.
